newsitem.title: USA: CME sets June 9 start for mark cross-rate futures.
newsitem.headline: CME sets June 9 start for mark cross-rate futures.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Monday it will open pit and after-hours electronic trading June 9 in futures and futures-options based on sterling/mark and mark/yen currency cross-rates.
CME later plans to add futures and futures-options based on mark/Swiss franc and mark/French franc crosses.
Some of the new contracts are altered versions of currency cross-rate futures that CME launched in February 1992 and later pulled from the trading pits.
Modifications include larger contract sizes and physical delivery rather cash settlement, a CME spokesman said.
CME's cross-rate futures will be quoted in terms of a currency versus the mark except the sterling contract, which will be sized in pounds and quoted in marks, the CME said.

The sterling/mark contract will be based on 125,000 pounds and feature a minimum price change of 0.0001 mark per pound. The mark/yen cross-rate will be based on 250,000 marks, quoted in yen per mark and use a tick size of 0.005 yen per mark.

CME said the new cross-rate contracts will allow use of "delivery netting" procedures in which CME's clearinghouse can net cash flows at delivery if positions belong to the same beneficial account owner.

The CME also said its GLOBEX Foreign Exchange Facility received regulatory approval to make markets on request in the cross-rate futures during pit-trading hours. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
